method: Each open string is read as a note name, optional accidental and octave and converted to a MIDI note number. A capo adds its fret number to every open string, and each displayed fret adds one semitone, so fret numbers are counted from the capo and fret 0 is the capo itself. Pitch classes come from a twelve-name table with sharps or flats selected by the spelling setting, and the octave is the MIDI number divided by twelve, rounded down, minus one. Positions for the selected note are every string and fret whose pitch class matches, reported per string in tuning order. Presets cover standard, drop D, DADGAD, open G and 7-string guitar, 4- and 5-string bass, high-G and low-G ukulele and mandolin; a custom tuning accepts one to eight strings written top row first, each with a note and octave. The fret count is a whole number from 1 to 24 and the capo from 0 to 12, and any tuning, capo and fret combination that would exceed MIDI note 127 is refused.

sources.title: Standard guitar tuning is E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4 from the lowest string to the highest, with twelve equal semitones per octave.
Scientific pitch notation names middle C as C4, which is MIDI note 60; each semitone is one MIDI note number.
A capo clamps across the fingerboard at a chosen fret and raises every open string by that many semitones, so shapes are counted relative to the capo.
